items.description: Sec. 4.1 never says which boundary is fixed. It only calls the problem a 'classic 2D cantilever beam', puts the load on the right edge, and later mentions 'fixed-boundary corners'. The actual support is drawn only in the Fig. 3 'problem setup (bottom left)' panel, which is not available.
readings: Entire left edge fixed (x = 0, 0 <= y <= H)
Only a central segment of the left edge fixed (e.g., 0.25H <= y <= 0.75H)
Only short segments at the top and bottom ends of the left edge fixed (e.g., y <= 0.1H and y >= 0.9H)

items.entity: constraint type on the fixed (left) edge
items.description: Sec. 4.1 does not say which displacement components are held. 'Cantilever' suggests full clamping, and Sec. 4.3 uses 'fully clamped' for a different case, but for this example the constraint type appears only in Fig. 3.
readings: Fully clamped: u_x = u_y = 0 at every node of the fixed edge
Roller: u_x = 0 along the edge, with u_y = 0 at a single node only (e.g., mid-height or a corner)

items.entity: 100 MPa traction on the right edge: location along the edge
items.description: Sec. 4.1 says only 'apply a 100 MPa traction to the right edge'. Sec. 4.4, referring back to 'the purely structural cantilever of Section 4.1', says the traction is 'applied at the center of the right edge'. The exact location is shown only in the Fig. 3 setup.
readings: Centered at mid-height of the right edge (x = L, y = 0.5H)
At the bottom-right corner (x = L, y = 0), as in the common textbook cantilever
Spread over the whole right edge (resultant at y = 0.5H)

items.entity: loaded length and distribution of the right-edge traction
items.description: In Sec. 4.1, 'traction to the right edge' reads as loading the whole 100 mm edge. Sec. 4.4's 'at the center of the right edge' implies a small patch. The patch length (number of loaded element faces) is never given, and neither is whether the load is a uniform traction or a lumped nodal force.
readings: Uniform 100 MPa over the full right edge (100 mm)
Uniform 100 MPa over a 2 mm patch (two element faces) centered at y = 0.5H
Uniform 100 MPa over a 10 mm patch, 0.45H <= y <= 0.55H
Uniform 100 MPa over a 20 mm patch, 0.4H <= y <= 0.6H
Equivalent single nodal force at the mid-height node

items.description: Sec. 4.1 gives only the magnitude. The direction (across the beam or along its axis, and its sign) is not stated anywhere for this case and appears only in the Fig. 3 setup. 'Downward' is stated only for the different clamped-clamped case in Sec. 4.3.
readings: Vertical, downward (-y) shear traction
Vertical, upward (+y); gives the same linear-compliance optimum as downward
Horizontal, normal to the edge (+x or -x, axial tension or compression)

items.entity: total (resultant) force of the right-edge load
items.description: Only the traction intensity (100 MPa) and the plane-stress thickness (1 mm, Sec. 4 defaults) are given. The total force or nodal-force values a solver needs depend on the loaded length, which is not given (see the load extent item). For a fixed load distribution, the total force only scales the compliance.
readings: 10,000 N (100 MPa x 100 mm x 1 mm, full edge)
2,000 N (20 mm patch)
1,000 N (10 mm patch)
200 N (2 mm patch)

items.description: Neither Sec. 4.1 nor the Sec. 4 defaults mention passive elements, such as a solid pad under the loaded patch or a solid strip along the clamped edge. The Fig. 3 setup panel may show them.
readings: None: all 200 x 100 elements are design variables
Small solid non-design pad under the loaded patch on the right edge (e.g., 1-5 element layers)
Solid non-design strip along the fixed left edge

items.entity: volume constraint V* = 0.5: which density field is constrained
items.description: Eq. (19) integrates the raw design variable rho. Sec. 3.2 says the filtered density is the physical density passed to the FE analysis. The text does not say which field the 0.5 limit applies to; the two differ near the domain boundaries with the normalized cone filter.
readings: Mean of raw design densities rho <= 0.5
Mean of filtered physical densities rho_tilde <= 0.5

items.description: No starting density is given for the 2D examples. Only the 3D blade's starting composition, theta = (0.5, 0.5), is stated (Sec. 4.5). With RAMP q = 8 the problem is non-convex, so the starting point can change which local optimum is reached.
readings: Uniform rho = V* = 0.5
Uniform rho = 1 (fully solid)
Uniform rho at another value, or with a random perturbation

items.description: J_el = f_ext^T u_0 is optimized with MMA using 'default parameters' (Sec. 3.4), but no scaling of the objective is stated. Sec. 4.3 itself attributes differences between topologies to 'MMA sensitivity to objective magnitude'.
readings: Raw J_el in N*mm (mJ)
J_el divided by its value at the initial design
J_el multiplied by a fixed constant (e.g., 1e-3 or 1e3)

items.description: Sec. 3.5 says the procedure stops 'when the design and objective change fall below a prescribed tolerance', with no objective tolerance given. Sec. 4 says it stops after 250 iterations or when max|rho_i - rho_(i-1)| <= 1e-5, which checks design change only.
readings: Stop at 250 iterations or when the max design change <= 1e-5 (design change only)
Also stop when the relative objective change falls below a tolerance, e.g., 1e-4
Also stop when the relative objective change falls below a tolerance, e.g., 1e-6

locator: Sec. 4.1, the structural cantilever baseline design minimizing elastic compliance (Fig. 3)
